evidence: The hunk shows both the H1 title and the Spec file field carrying `/Users/bmf/code/...`; commit 1cbf6f5 replaced only the Scope-section path, leaving the H1 line that F5 then flagged.
guidance_note: When a reviewer flags a leaked absolute path, grep the whole file (and sibling reports) for the prefix `/Users/` and fix every hit, not only the quoted line.

evidence: Same absolute path in 2-spec.md lines 1 and 4; 1cbf6f5 changed only line 4 (`- Spec file: `SPEC.md``), leaving `# Audit: /Users/bmf/...` on line 1.
guidance_note: Grep for the leaked prefix across the whole file before replying Applied, since the reviewer's comment explicitly said 'and similarly'.

evidence: The header read 'Spec sections not examined:' while every bullet said 'examined'; 1cbf6f5 renamed it and added an explicit 'not examined: none' line plus a template split.
guidance_note: Have audit subagents fill a template whose section headers are unambiguous (examined vs not-examined) before the report is written.

evidence: Checklist item 4 was `- [ ]` with future-tense text while the PR description said the epic was created; 1cbf6f5 checked it and named tmux-audit-x5u and its children.
guidance_note: Update durable plan checklists in the same commit that completes the step the PR description claims done.

evidence: 1cbf6f5's diff for 1-spec-manifest.md touches only line 4; line 1 still reads `# Audit: /Users/bmf/code/tmux-control-mode-js/SPEC_MANIFEST.md`, and the agent conceded 'the title line was missed'.
guidance_note: After fixing one instance of a leaked path, grep the file for the same prefix before pushing.

evidence: 1cbf6f5 changed only the Spec file line of 2-spec.md; the H1 `# Audit: /Users/bmf/code/tmux-control-mode-js/SPEC.md` was untouched.
guidance_note: After fixing one instance of a leaked path, grep the file for the same prefix before pushing.

evidence: The 'yields 27 ... = 28 actually' sentence is in the original report text; 1cbf6f5 only shifted its line number (288 to 290) by inserting the examined/not-examined lines, so the ON-POST-REVIEW-COMMIT flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: Spot-check subagent-written audit reports for self-contradicting numbers (a count stated then re-derived) before opening the PR.

narrative: Audit-artifact PR with four valid documentation findings in round 0, all accepted. The path fix covered only the Scope field, so round 1 re-flagged the H1 titles in both reports. Round 1 also caught a pre-existing 27/28 miscount that was not fix-caused, so round 1 would have happened anyway, and round 2 was clean.
guidance_observations: The reviewer said 'and similarly' in F1/F2, but the agent fixed only the quoted line. Treating a reviewer's 'similarly' as a sweep instruction would have removed two findings.
Subagent-written audit reports went out without a self-consistency read, and the reviewer caught the 27/28 contradiction instead.

evidence: The invariant said the only %-prefixed lines in a block are terminators, while the rationale cited `%5` output from list-panes inside a block, which is a direct contradiction; 492fe6b reframed it as notifications never interleaved.
guidance_note: When promoting a parenthetical to a named invariant, restate exactly the upstream claim (tmux.1: 'a notification will never occur inside a response block') rather than a stronger paraphrase.

evidence: The parser comment repeated the same over-strong rule and then relied on `%5` being in-block output; 492fe6b rewrote it to position-based routing. The fix did not sweep the class docstring or the onOutputLine doc in the same file, and F3 flagged those.
guidance_note: When correcting how a concept is described, grep the file for every other doc site that describes the same rule (here 'start with %') and rewrite them together.

evidence: 492fe6b's parser.ts diff touches only the inline [LAW] block. The class docstring (~289-290) and onOutputLine doc (~301-302) still describe in-block output as lines that do not start with `%`, which the agent confirmed.
guidance_note: When fixing a comment's framing of a rule, search the file for the old framing ('not start with %') and fix every site in the same commit.

narrative: Spec/comment PR naming a block-purity invariant. Round 0 rightly found that the invariant and the parser comment contradicted their own `%5` example, and both were reworded. The reword hit only one of three doc sites in parser.ts, so round 1 flagged the other two. Round 2 was clean.
guidance_observations: The original PR introduced an invariant stronger than the upstream quote it cited. Checking the paraphrase against the quoted source before opening would have avoided round 0's findings.
A same-file grep for the old framing during the F2 fix would have made round 1 unnecessary.

evidence: tcgetattr needs a terminal device (ENOTTY otherwise), and a PTY is one kind of tty, so 'requires a PTY-backed file descriptor' over-specifies. The agent reworded it to 'a tty (a PTY is the typical kind...)'.

The reviewer noted spawnTmux uses `stdio: ["pipe","pipe","ignore"]`, so the quoted stderr string never reaches consumers, and the agent confirmed this and dropped the quote. Locale-dependent strerror wording also makes the quote non-deterministic.
guidance_note: Before quoting an error string in a spec, check whether the transport surfaces that stream at all (here stderr is ignored).

evidence: This is the same PTY-vs-tty over-specification mirrored in SPEC_MANIFEST §2.1 ('fails unless stdin is PTY-backed'), and it got the same reword.
guidance_note: When a spec statement is mirrored across two layers, write it once and copy it, so a correction in one is a correction in both.

narrative: Small spec PR documenting the spawnTmux -CC refusal. Round 0 raised three accurate precision findings (tty vs PTY twice, and a stderr quote that the default transport discards). All were fixed in one commit, and round 1 was clean.
guidance_observations: Fixing the mirrored section in the same pass as the original kept this PR to a single fix round.

evidence: The client fans out one Uint8Array instance to every sink, and the original write JSDoc said nothing about mutation or retention. The fix added read-only/no-retain text, but it was overstated ('not retained by the library after write returns'), which F12 later flagged, and the repo's own recording sink violated it (F7).
guidance_note: When adding a contract clause (MUST NOT retain), grep the PR's own test fixtures and sibling code for violations of it, and state the retention window precisely in the same edit.

evidence: With a Set registry and an end() per disposer, sharing a sink across attachments double-fired end(). Instead of forbidding reuse, the agent made attachments structurally independent via per-call symbol keys, which removes the hazard the reviewer named.
guidance_note: Design the registry key around the lifecycle unit (the attachment, not the sink instance) before writing per-attachment lifecycle docs.

evidence: `sinks.add(sink)` on a Set de-dupes a repeated attach while each disposer calls `sink.end?.()`. The agent took the reviewer's option (b), per-attachment tokens in a `Map<symbol, PaneByteSink>`, and added a regression test.
guidance_note: When a disposer has per-call side effects (end()), key the registry by a per-call token from the start.

evidence: Iterating a live Set while a sink's write() mutates it can deliver the current chunk to new members. The fix snapshotted with Array.from, but it put the snapshot inside dispatchToPaneSinks, which runs after emit, so it missed handler-side mutation (F6).
guidance_note: When adding a 'membership fixed at arrival' snapshot, take it at the top of the message frame, before any user callback (emit or sink) can run, and test each mutation source.

evidence: The test name claimed end() is called exactly once while the sink omits end; the agent renamed it to 'tolerates sinks that omit the optional end() method'.
guidance_note: Read each test name against its assertions before opening the PR.

evidence: The F4 fix's comment promised 'membership is fixed to what was attached when this chunk arrived', but the snapshot ran after `this.emitter.emit(msg)`, so an output handler's attach back-filled. The flag commit d7cacf6 was only a formatting change. The defect is the F4 fix's snapshot placement, fixed in bfff885 with a pre-emit snapshot and two tests.
guidance_note: When fixing a mutation-during-iteration bug, enumerate every callback that can mutate the registry in the same frame (sinks and emit listeners) and place the snapshot before all of them.

evidence: The F1 fix added 'MUST NOT be retained past the synchronous write call', while createRecordingSink still did `chunks.push(bytes)`. The PR's own fixture violated the contract the fix introduced, and bfff885 changed it to `bytes.slice()`.
guidance_note: After adding a contract rule to an interface, grep the PR's implementations and test doubles of that interface for violations.

evidence: Pre-fix dispatchToPaneSinks returned early when `attachments === undefined`. bfff885 replaced that with `Array.from(this.paneSinks.get(msg.paneId)?.values() ?? [])` plus a wrapper object for every output message, which added an allocation on the hot path. The types law is decoration on a perf fix.
guidance_note: When restructuring a hot-path function, keep its existing early-exit for the empty case and diff the allocation profile against the old code.

evidence: The JSDoc claimed a throwing sink surfaces 'on the next message' and 'may detach silently', but the code calls sink.write with no try/catch, so the throw propagates immediately. bfff885 (flagged) did not touch pane-sink.ts, so the text predates that commit and the flag is a false positive. The packet does not show whether the text came from the original PR or 2b3ea69. The law token is pasted onto a comment-accuracy fix.
guidance_note: Write failure-mode docs by tracing the actual call path (no try/catch around write, so it propagates synchronously), not by guessing at behavior.

evidence: emit ran before sink dispatch in the original code and in every fix since, and 69562dd (flagged) only extracted computePaneDispatch, so the ordering is pre-review. The reviewer had already offered 'or dispatch before emit' in F6, and the agent passed on it. single-enforcer does not govern call ordering.
guidance_note: When a reviewer offers two fixes for an ordering bug (snapshot before emit, or dispatch before emit), check whether the second also closes the throwing-listener failure mode before choosing one.

evidence: 5b9adb9 moved sink dispatch before `this.emitter.emit(msg)`, but the PR description still said sinks run after emit, and the agent confirmed this and updated the description.
guidance_note: When a fix changes a behavior the PR description states, update the description in the same push.

evidence: The F1 fix wrote 'not retained by the library after write returns' and 'The library never reads bytes again after dispatch', but later sinks in the snapshot see the same buffer. After 5b9adb9, emit also reads it after sink dispatch. e7f32e8 restated the retention window as the chunk's synchronous frame.
guidance_note: When writing a buffer-ownership clause, state the library's actual retention window (the whole fan-out frame) rather than the per-call view.

evidence: The fake transport's no-op send/onClose type-checks via arity subtyping, and no test in the suite uses close or send, so the 'silent drift' is hypothetical. e7f32e8 (flagged) did not touch the test file, so the flag is a false positive on original code. The law is about asserting behavior, not double fidelity.
guidance_note: Reuse the repo's existing fake transport (tests/unit/connection-state.test.ts) instead of hand-rolling a degenerate one in each new suite.

narrative: A new sink API with seven review rounds. The F4 snapshot fix sat after emit, so handler-side mutation still back-filled (F6). The F6 fix dropped the empty-pane early exit and added a hot-path allocation (F8). The F1 contract text was violated by the PR's own test fixture (F7) and overstated the retention window (F12), and the F10 reorder left the PR description stale (F11). Rounds 1 and 4 contained only fix-caused findings. F9, F10 and F13 were pre-existing issues that the reviewer surfaced late.
guidance_observations: Each fix was scoped to the quoted line rather than to the invariant it claimed (snapshot placement, contract compliance across fixtures), which produced a fix-caused finding in most rounds.
In F6 the reviewer offered 'dispatch before emit', and taking it would have closed F10 two rounds earlier. Evaluate every alternative a reviewer lists, not just the first.
Law tokens were attached to perf and doc-accuracy fixes where they did no work (F8, F9, F10, F12).

evidence: PaneEndEnvelope carries only paneId, so the first paneEnd detaches every receiver for that pane. The agent took the reviewer's 'enforce single attachment' option with a constructor-time registry. The fix still returned a reusable PaneByteSink, so the 'unrepresentable' claim was false, and F2 caught exactly that.
guidance_note: When enforcing 'one attachment per key', enforce it at the point of attachment (own the attachPaneSink call), not at sink construction, because the returned sink can still be attached repeatedly.

evidence: bc63bea's createWebContentsSink returned a PaneByteSink whose end() freed the slot and sent paneEnd. Attaching that sink twice via attachPaneSink still raced, which the agent conceded ('the round-1 fix only guarded the constructor'). d3fe9ae's attachWebContentsSink owns the attach call and returns only a disposer.
guidance_note: Before claiming an illegal state is unrepresentable, list every value the API returns and check whether any of them can recreate that state.

evidence: d3fe9ae renamed createWebContentsSink to attachWebContentsSink but left the errors.ts doc naming createWebContentsSink. The agent's own later `grep -rn createWebContentsSink` was the sweep that should have run in d3fe9ae.
guidance_note: When renaming a public function, run `grep -rn <oldName> src/ tests/` and fix every hit in the rename commit.

evidence: The IPC.paneEnd doc still said it fires 'when the disposer returned from attachPaneSink runs'. After d3fe9ae, the consumer-facing disposer is attachWebContentsSink's, and 215cef2 updated it.
guidance_note: When an API refactor changes which call the consumer makes, grep docs for the old lifecycle description as well as the old name.

evidence: renderer.ts still said 'Renderer-side companion to `createWebContentsSink`' and had a matching @see after d3fe9ae removed that export. 215cef2's diff shows both lines changed.
guidance_note: When renaming a public function, run `grep -rn <oldName> src/ tests/` and fix every hit in the rename commit.

evidence: The types.ts envelope comment named createWebContentsSink as the importer after the rename. 215cef2 changed it to attachWebContentsSink.
guidance_note: When renaming a public function, run `grep -rn <oldName> src/ tests/` and fix every hit in the rename commit.

evidence: d3fe9ae wrote 'The slot is freed when the returned disposer is called (or when the library fires end() for any other reason)', but in the same commit it moved `registrySet.delete(paneId)` out of end() into the disposer. The flag names 215cef2, but the clause was authored in d3fe9ae.
guidance_note: After moving a side effect between functions, reread the docblock of both functions for claims about where that side effect happens.

narrative: Round 0 correctly found that paneId-only envelopes cannot separate concurrent attachments. The first fix guarded only sink construction and still returned a reusable sink, so round 1 re-raised the same race. The proper fix (attachWebContentsSink owning the attachment) renamed the API without sweeping references, which produced four stale-name findings in round 2. It also left a lifecycle clause contradicting its own code move, flagged in round 3. Every round after the first came from the previous fix.
guidance_observations: The agent claimed [LAW:types-are-the-program] unrepresentability for a runtime constructor check while still returning a misusable value. Checking the claim against the returned values would have gone straight to the d3fe9ae design.
The rename sweep (`grep -rn createWebContentsSink`) ran only after the reviewer found the stale names. Running it in the rename commit would have removed a round.

evidence: The docstring said Electron's WebContents race is 'mitigated the same way in the bridge's wsSend chokepoint', but wsSend lives in the websocket server.ts and the Electron path uses wc.isDestroyed(). The agent called the sentence nonsense and reworded it to point at ./server.ts.
guidance_note: When writing a cross-reference to a mitigation in another module, open that module and confirm the named function exists there before citing it.

narrative: WebSocket sink PR modeled on the settled Electron design. Round 0 raised a single valid finding about a wrong cross-module reference in a docstring, fixed in one commit, and round 1 was clean.
guidance_observations: Reusing the shape #53 settled on after review (own the attachment, return only a disposer) meant no design findings here.
